The weather there is very dry and my hands were dry and the finger tips were cracking and even bleeding.  While it didn't solve the bleeding finger tips (a derm doctor had a solution for that)  it did the absolute best job of keeping the natural moisture in my hands.  I use to use the Neutragena Fisherman's hand cream and swore by it until I found this cream.  It is cheaper and not as thick as the Fisherman's hand cream.  Glad Amazon is now carrying as it has been out of stock for nearly two years, at least in the smaller 1.7 oz size.  It functions like a barrier-repair cream allowing the skin to repair itself.  Takes a few minutes to absorb, but it is well worth it.  I limit it to the back of my hands as the gylcerin in the product can make your fingers a little slippery and like most cream can leave finger prints on glass, screen, etc.  The only other truly outstanding cream out there is Cerave which is also very moderately priced considering the expensive cermindes they put into it.  You can buy a big tub of the stuff for under $13.00.
